excerpt: OSARO is a San Francisco company whose machine-learning software lets warehouse robots pick, bag, kit and depalletise items. Products, funding and alternatives.
content:
OSARO builds AI software and robotic systems for warehouses and distribution centres. Its machine-learning vision lets industrial robot arms handle tasks that used to need people because every item looks different: picking individual products out of totes, putting orders into bags, assembling kits and unloading pallets. The company's about page lists OSARO SightWorks, its vision and control software, alongside robotic piece-picking, bagging, kitting and depalletisation systems and a post-installation support programme called HyperCare. Its systems work with existing automation such as automated storage and retrieval systems, mobile robots and conveyors, The Robot Report noted.

OSARO was founded in 2015, according to The Robot Report, and is based at 500 3rd Street in San Francisco. Its co-founders are Derik Pridmore, the CEO, who the company says was an early investor in DeepMind and Clarifai, and Michael Kahane, the CTO. OSARO lists four granted US patents. The Robot Report reported in 2021 that it had dozens of customers across five continents and deployments in seven countries.

On funding, OSARO announced a $16 million Series B in 2019 with investors including King River Capital, Alpha Intelligence Capital and Founders Fund, bringing total funding to $29.3 million. In August 2021 it raised a $30 million Series C led by Octave Ventures, with J17 Capital, Tomales Bay Capital and existing investors AME Cloud Ventures, iRobot, King River Capital and Founders Fund, for total funding of $67.5 million.

OSARO does not publish prices. Systems are scoped for each warehouse and quoted after a consultation.

This page is research, not a review. We have not tested OSARO's robots; facts come from its website and the reporting under Sources.
